# Summary of 2015 UK Election Manifesto

## Economic Policy

The manifesto commits to reducing the deficit annually and achieving a balanced budget, with all proposals fully funded without additional borrowing. Key fiscal measures include maintaining competitive corporate tax rates, closing tax loopholes, abolishing non-domiciled tax status, and introducing a property tax on homes valued over £2 million. Business rates would be cut and frozen for smaller businesses.

## Employment and Wages

Proposals include raising the minimum wage to over £8 per hour by 2019, banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, and promoting the Living Wage through government procurement. A jobs guarantee program would provide paid employment for long-term unemployed young people and adults.

## Education and Skills

The manifesto proposes reducing university tuition fees from £9,000 to £6,000, guaranteeing apprenticeships for qualifying school leavers, and protecting education budgets. All state school teachers would require qualified teacher status, with class sizes capped at 30 for younger children.

## Healthcare

Plans include recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, 20,000 nurses, and 3,000 midwives, funded through property taxes and tobacco levies. The manifesto promises GP appointments within 48 hours and equal priority for mental and physical health services, while integrating health and social care provision.

## Housing

Targets include building 200,000 homes annually by 2020, introducing three-year tenancies with rent increase caps for private renters, and abolishing letting agent fees. The so-called "Bedroom Tax" would be abolished.

## Families and Childcare

Free childcare would expand from 15 to 25 hours weekly for working parents of three and four-year-olds. Paternity leave would double to four weeks with increased pay.

## Immigration

Proposals include hiring 1,000 additional border staff, requiring two-year residency before benefit eligibility for migrants, and making it illegal to undercut wages through worker exploitation.

## Devolution and Constitutional Reform

Major devolution of £30 billion to English regions is proposed, alongside extended powers for Scotland and Wales. The voting age would be lowered to 16, and the upper legislative chamber would be replaced with an elected regional senate.

## International Affairs

The manifesto supports continued international alliance membership and proposes reforming rather than leaving regional partnerships. Defense commitments include maintaining nuclear deterrent capabilities while pursuing multilateral disarmament. Climate change is prioritized, with commitments to international development spending at 0.7% of national income.
